description: (0.5.0) Forced DID-document re-fetch (RFC-ACDP-0001 §5.11 'Caching', 'Rate-limited re-fetch', 'Freshness is per operation'). A verifier holding a cached DID document re-fetches once, bypassing the cache, before reporting a step-4 or step-5 failure or classifying a revocation candidate as permanently invalid. A re-fetch declined by rate limiting makes a step-4 absence transient, never permanent.

input.setup: The consumer first resolves P's DID document with only K1. P then adds K2 (verificationMethod and assertionMethod) and publishes a body signed by K2.

expected.behavior: Verification of the K2-signed body triggers exactly one cache-bypassing fetch of P's DID document, then succeeds. It MUST NOT fail with key_resolution_failed from the stale document.

scenarios.name: B — re-fetch declined by the rate limit

expected.behavior: The forced re-fetch for P is already used up (for example, an attacker published bodies naming bogus fragments under P), and the K2-signed candidate is a revocation of K1. The verdict is key_resolution_unreachable (transient) and the discovery outcome unknown — never a permanently invalid candidate or not-revoked.
Several candidates in one discovery run name keys missing from P's cached document. Exactly one forced fetch of P's DID happens in that run; the fresh document serves every candidate.
